However, the vibration level on the motor side increased by about thirty percent during the last fifty hours. We suspect the bearing, but we cannot be sure until we open the unit. So my suggestion is to stop the test now and inspect the bearing, rather than risk a failure.

audio: The reason we chose aluminium for the frame is not the cost. In fact, steel would have been cheaper. The main reason is the weight: the robot arm has to accelerate very quickly, and every extra kilogram means a bigger motor. The drawback is stiffness. Aluminium bends about three times more than steel, so we had to make the sections deeper to compensate.

questions.q: Why was aluminium chosen?

Because it is easier to weld.

audio: What caught us out was not the stiffness of the panel itself, which matched the model within a few percent, but the way it was mounted. We had assumed the brackets were rigid. In reality they were flexible enough to drop the first natural frequency from sixty hertz to forty five, right into the range of the compressor. Had we tested the whole assembly rather than the panel alone, we would have spotted it months earlier.

questions.q: What was the source of the problem?
options: The panel was not stiff enough.
The model of the panel was wrong.
The mounting brackets were more flexible than assumed.

questions.q: What does the speaker regret?
